newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says employee contracts remains intact in transfers.
newsitem.headline: Court says employee contracts remains intact in transfers.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday that when an undertaking is sold, its employees are automatically transferred to the purchaser as of the date of transfer, despite the intention of the seller or buyer.
The new undertaking must recognize the employee contract held with the former undertaking.

"The directive is intended to safeguard the rights of workers in the event of a change of employer by making it possible for them to continue to work for the new employer under the same conditions as those agreed with the transferor," the court said.

The issue arose in a dispute between employees claiming wrongful dismissal against I.G.C. Housing services, which took over the operations of their former employer, J. Benoidt SA after it went into liquidation.

The employees were dismissed with six months notice immediately after the first company went into liquidation, but were told to work through the notice with the new company. After challenging the change in job functions, the employees were laid off by the liquidator.
The court reasoned that if the transferee of the employment contracts may alter or end employment contracts, the intention of the directive would be defeated.
(EXCERPT FROM THE JUDGMENT)
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: French)

"Safeguarding of employees' rights in the event of transfers of undertakings, businesses or parts of businesses - Transfer to the transferree of the rights and obligations arising from a contract of employment - Date of transfer"
In Case C 305/94
Reference from the Tribunal du Travail, Brussels, for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between
Claude Rotsart de Hertaing
and
J. Benoidt SA, in liquidation
and
I.G.C. Housing Service SA

on the interpretation of Council directive 77/187/EEC of 14 February 1977 onthe approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the safeguarding of employees' rights in the event of transfers of undertakings, businesses or parts of businesses (OJ 1977 L 61, p. 26)
THE COURT hereby rules

1. Article 3(1) of Council directive 77/187/EEC of 14 February 1977 on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the safeguarding of employees' rights in the event of transfers of undertakings, businesses or parts of businesses is to be interpreted as meaning that the contracts of employment and employment relationships existing on the date of the transfer of an undertaking between the transferor and the workers employed in the undertaking transferred are automatically transferred from the transferor to the transferee by the mere fact of the transfer of the undertaking, despite the contrary intention of the transferor or tranferee and despite the latter's refusal to fulfil his obligations.

2. The transfer of the contracts of employment and employment relationships pursuant to article 3(1) of directive 77/187 necessarily takes place on the date of the transfer of the undertaking and cannot be postpoined to another date at the will of the transferor or transferee.
